title: Retention sweep deletes drafts on vacancy archive, contradicting the 'link works until the vacancy closes' promise and risking permanent loss on a transient state
evidence: +DELETE FROM application_draft d +USING vacancy v +WHERE d.vacancy_id = v.id + AND ( + v.status = 'closed' + OR v.archived_at IS NOT NULL + OR (v.closes_at IS NOT NULL AND v.closes_at <= now()) + ) +RETURNING d.id::text; vs the continue-link email copy in this same chunk: + "This link works until the vacancy closes on " + <> escape_html(format_close_date(closes_on)) + <> ""."
detail: Archive is a distinct condition from close (the SQL lists them separately), and the chunk's own comment says an archived vacancy merely 'stops accepting'. The daily sweep permanently deletes drafts the moment a vacancy is archived; if it later returns to active, saved answers and emailed continue links are dead despite the 'until the vacancy closes' promise.
recommended_fix: Delete drafts only on closed/closes_at; either leave archived-vacancy drafts until close, or sweep them only after an archive-age threshold (e.g. 30 days) so short archives don't wipe in-progress applicants.

title: Unauthenticated draft-save endpoint has no per-vacancy or aggregate bound — fabricated-email rows accumulate until vacancy close
evidence:
+////   - The save endpoint writes but never reads back: worst case an attacker
+////     stores field values against an email they don't own, visible only to
+////     whoever holds that inbox (the continue link goes to the email, not
+////     the requester).

and
+INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields)
+VALUES ($1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb)
+ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
detail: The abuse model considers only PII visibility, not volume. The upsert keys on (vacancy, email), so invented emails yield unlimited rows up to ~64 KB each; nothing in the chunk rate-limits the write, and retention sweeps only at vacancy close — an open vacancy's draft table can be bloated indefinitely.
recommended_fix: Add a per-vacancy draft cap (reject new keys past N) and/or a per-IP throttle on /apply/:code/draft; the 64 KB body cap alone does not bound row count.

title: strip_draft_on_submit email is not trimmed, but the draft-save path trims — a whitespace mismatch leaves the draft PII unstripped
evidence:
+      case
+        sql.strip_draft_on_submit(
+          db,
+          vacancy_uuid,
+          get_form_value(values, "email"),
+        )

vs draft_handler save path:
+      let applicant_email = string.trim(payload.email)
detail: Drafts are keyed on lower(trim(email)); the strip matches lower($2) with no visible trim on the submit-side value. If the final form value isn't normalized elsewhere, leading/trailing whitespace makes the UPDATE match nothing and the pre-submit PII payload lingers until vacancy close.
recommended_fix: Trim the form email before calling strip_draft_on_submit (or lower(trim($2)) in the SQL) so the strip key is byte-identical to the upsert key.

title: continue-link 'sent' flag is a submission-status oracle, contradicting the 'never reveals' comment
evidence:
+/// Always 200
+/// on well-formed payloads: the response never reveals whether a draft or
+/// mailbox exists

vs the claim SQL:
+WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
+  AND email = lower($2)
+  AND submitted_at IS NULL

and
+                    Ok(pog.Returned(_, [])) ->
+                      wisp.json_response(
+                        json_ok_with([#("sent", json.bool(False))]),
+                        200,
+                      )
detail: Anyone knowing the applicant's email + vacancy code can poll with an empty fields map (skips upsert, claims against the existing draft). sent:true flips to permanent sent:false exactly when the victim submits — the response does reveal something the header comment claims it never does.
recommended_fix: Answer sent:true even when the claim returns zero rows (the client copy already reads cooldown and sent identically); keep ok:false only for genuine send failures.

title: 'Always 200 on well-formed payloads' is false: claim DB failure returns 500 while upsert DB failure returns 200
detail: Two DB failures on identical, well-formed requests produce different status codes (200 vs 500), and the 500 contradicts the endpoint's own 'Always 200' doc line. The client's retry/'try again' behaviour now depends on which internal call failed.
recommended_fix: Pick one posture — return ok:false/200 for both failure modes (matching the doc), or 500 for both, and update the comment.

title: Comment claims stage-2 email without continue_url is 'byte-identical to the pre-F3 stage 2', but the shared checklist copy changed in the same diff
evidence:
+  // F3×E2 seam: when the enquirer has a live draft, the CTA becomes the
+  // tokenized continue-link (tracked as its own template so the funnel can
+  // separate continue-clicks from fresh-start clicks); otherwise the email
+  // is byte-identical to the pre-F3 stage 2.

vs the requirements_checklist_html() change both branches call:
-  <> "The form is completed in one visit — it doesn't save your progress — so it's worth gathering everything before you open it."
+  <> "You don’t have to finish in one visit — on the form you can save your progress and email yourself a link to pick up where you left off."
detail: Both branches of the stage-2 builder call requirements_checklist_html(), whose closing paragraph was rewritten in this PR — so the no-continue_url email is not byte-identical to pre-F3. The comment misleads anyone verifying the funnel split.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment to 'identical except the CTA/saved-line' (the checklist change applies to both variants), or drop the byte-identical claim.

title: Submit-time strip only matches the final form email — drafts keyed under an earlier/edited email keep their PII
detail: Drafts are keyed per (vacancy, email); a typo then correction, or editing the email field after saves, creates a second draft row. The strip at finalise targets only the submitted email, so the earlier row's field payload survives until vacancy close with no continue-link owner aware of it.
recommended_fix: Strip all draft rows for the vacancy matching any email the applicant used this session, or add an applicant-side sweep/TTL for stale unsubmitted drafts independent of the final submit email.

title: get_draft_by_continue_token selects resumed_at and vacancy_id that no handler in the chunk reads
evidence:
+SELECT
+  d.id::text,
+  d.vacancy_id::text,
+  d.email,
+  d.fields::text,
+  COALESCE(d.resumed_at::text, '') AS resumed_at,
+  COALESCE(d.submitted_at::text, '') AS submitted_at

handlers use only draft.id, draft.email, draft.fields, draft.submitted_at
detail: Two decoded row fields are never consumed by resume, erasure-confirm, or erasure-delete. Harmless but dead surface in a generated row type that every future reader must reason about.
recommended_fix: Drop vacancy_id and resumed_at from the SELECT/row type, or use them (e.g. vacancy_id to cross-check the route code instead of the JOIN alone).
